# Same-coset mixed Brunn--Minkowski and its peak refinement

This is an exact finite-source volume inequality. It is not a depth
theorem or a parity-decimation monotonicity assertion. In particular,
no union of overlapping midpoint fibers is charged more than once.

Let d>=1. Let A and B be nonempty finite unions of compact convex
continuous fibers in R^n x R^d, with bases in Z^n. Their mixed measure
is the sum of d-dimensional fiber volumes. Write their masses M_A,M_B
and largest fiber volumes a,b. Initially assume M_A,M_B>0.

Take 0<lambda<1 such that every base combination

    (1-lambda)p+lambda q

of a base p of A and a base q of B is integral. This holds for
lambda=1/2 if both base sets lie in the SAME parity class. More
generally it holds for lambda=j/m if both lie in one common residue
class modulo m. Let T=(1-lambda)A+lambda B. This has finitely many
integer bases and compact measurable fibers, although a T-fiber can
be a nonconvex finite union of convex sets.

Then the exact peak-sensitive bound is

    mu(T) >= max(M_A/a,M_B/b)
                 [(1-lambda)a^(1/d)+lambda b^(1/d)]^d,          (1)

and consequently

    mu(T)^(1/d) >= (1-lambda)M_A^(1/d)+lambda M_B^(1/d).        (2)

## Proof of (1)

Fix a base q of B whose fiber volume is b. For each base p of A
with positive fiber volume a_p, the T-fiber at (1-lambda)p+lambda q
contains (1-lambda)A_p+lambda B_q. Ordinary Brunn--Minkowski gives it
volume at least

    [(1-lambda)a_p^(1/d)+lambda b^(1/d)]^d.

These output bases are DISTINCT as p varies, since 1-lambda!=0.
Thus they may be summed without overlap between charged fibers.
For 0<a_p<=a, dividing the d-th root by a_p^(1/d) shows

    [(1-lambda)a_p^(1/d)+lambda b^(1/d)]^d
       >=(a_p/a)[(1-lambda)a^(1/d)+lambda b^(1/d)]^d.            (3)

Indeed the left root after that division is
(1-lambda)+lambda(b/a_p)^(1/d), which decreases as a_p increases.
Summing (3) proves the first term of the maximum in (1).

For the second term fix a largest fiber of A and vary q over the
positive fibers of B. The map q->(1-lambda)p+lambda q is again
injective, and the same argument with the roles interchanged gives
the second term. Each is a lower bound on the same mu(T); taking
their maximum proves (1). Their charged sets are NOT added together.

To deduce (2), put R=max(M_A/a,M_B/b). Then M_A<=R a and M_B<=R b,
so the right side of (2) is at most
R^(1/d)[(1-lambda)a^(1/d)+lambda b^(1/d)]. Use (1).

If one total mass is zero, fix any point in a fiber of that nonempty
set and translate/scalewise copy all positive fibers of the other set
into T. The same injectivity gives (2), with the zero term omitted.
If both masses are zero, (2) is trivial. The expression (1), which
divides by a and b, is used only when both masses are positive.
For lambda=0 or1, (2) is an identity and is handled separately.

For d=0 the corresponding direct assertion is
|T|>=max(|A|,|B|): fix a point of one set and use injectivity in the
other. No zero-dimensional root exponent or0^0 convention is used.

## Actual convex-body application and precise limits

If A and B are subsets of an actual convex body C with the stated
base congruence property, then T lies in C intersect (Z^n x R^d).
If A and B additionally lie in parallel caps {ell>=s} and {ell>=t},
then T lies in the cap {ell>=(1-lambda)s+lambda t}. Thus (1)-(2)
apply to those actual captured mixed volumes as well. Oblique affine
functionals ell are allowed; the containment is a pointwise affine
identity, not a statement restricted to fiber-parallel halfspaces.

The coefficient one in (2) is sharp: use one fiber for each input
and positive homothetic convex bodies in those fibers. Ordinary
Brunn--Minkowski is then equality and there is exactly one output base.

Crucially, the two inputs must have the stated integral combination
property. Arbitrary fibers of different parity cannot be averaged
and then counted as integer output fibers. Nor may (1) be summed
over several residue classes whose output sets overlap. No assertion
of one deterministic point of the required depth follows from (2)
alone. The archived parity-decimation, midpoint-tree, and parity-forest
cap-transport obstructions remain applicable. In particular this lemma
does not restore the false arbitrary-finite-base gamma_d/h(P) target.
